papers.paper: 2nd Semester B.Sc. Degree Examination (Machine Learning - CSC 572)
2nd Semester B.Sc. Degree Machine Learning - CSC 572 Test (1.5 hours)
2nd Semester Exam (CSC 572: Intro to Machine Learning)

questions.text:
(a) You are using gradient descent to find the minimum of the function f(x) = x². You experiment by fixing the number of iterations T and trying different learning rates to find the one which leads to a better (smaller) solution. There are different possible settings, e.g., you choose a learning rate of (1) zero; (2) the optimal learning rate; (3) a learning rate that is too large; (4) a learning rate that is too small. When initializing at point A on the plot below, which point of the plot are you most likely to reach with each learning rate setting?
Match the settings 1, 2, 3, and 4 to the points on the plot indicated by letters A, B, C, and D.
[Plot in the original paper: the curve f(x) = x² with points A and C on the right arm, B on the left arm and D at the minimum.]
1: learning rate of zero  2: optimal learning rate  3: too large learning rate  4: too small learning rate [8 marks]
(b). You are building a classifier for handwritten digit recognition and would be training your neural network model on the MNIST digit-recognition dataset. What activation function would you use for your model? [2 marks]

(a) You are working on a dataset that contains a categorical feature called "Education Level" with the following unique values: ["High School", "Bachelor's", "Master's", "PhD"]. You need to prepare this feature for use in a machine learning model.
i. Perform Label Encoding on the "Education Level" feature and show the result. [2 marks]
ii, Perform One-Hot Encoding on the "Education Level" feature and show the result. [2 marks]
ii. Which encoding method is more appropriate and why? [2 marks]
(b). What is the importance of min-max normalization and Bar chart in feature Engineering [4 marks]

A financial institution provides you with a dateset for building a fraud-detection classifier. The dataset contain 200,000 transaction records, each labeled as either Fraud or Not Fraud.
After performing exploratory data analysis, you discover that:
• 97% of the transactions are Not Fraud.
• 3% of the transactions are Fraud.
You are asked to train a machine learning model and evaluate its generalization performance using an appropriate cross-validation strategy.
a) Decide which evaluation strategy you will use and justify your choice by comparing it with at least one alternative evaluation approach. [4 marks]
b) Identify two performance metrics that are most appropriate for this task and explain why they provide better insight into model performance. [3 marks]
c) Suppose the model performs well on the majority class but poorly on the minority class. Describe two techniques you could apply during training to improve performance on the minority (Fraud) class. [3 marks]

Draw and label a typical neural network. [4 marks]
b) Explain in detail how a neural network learns. [6 marks]

Adaobi, the new lead of AI advocacy, seeks your expertise in applying Machine Learning to address different real-world problems.
a) For each of the problems listed below:
i. Determine what class and type of learning problem it is.
ii. Describe the kind of data needed to train the model.
iii. Propose a suitable algorithm for the task and explain why it is well-suited for this problem.
iv. What one underlying assumption does your recommended algorithm relies on?
➢ Sales Forecasting: Determine how much sales are possible in the 3rd quarter.
➢ Recommender systems: Suggest products or services to users.
➢ Sentiment analysis: Automatically determine whether a given text expresses positive, negative, or neutral sentiment.
➢ Spam email detection: Identify and filter out spam emails from a user's inbox. (2 marks each)
b) What is the relationship between sigmoid function and linear regressor? (2 marks)

(a)The figure below illustrates the decision boundary produced by a classifier from a learning algorithm. Analyze the plot and indicate the:
i) name of the learning algorithm.
ii) number of errors it makes on the training data.
Iii) express mathematically the default cost function used by the algorithm. (2 marks each)
[Figure in the original paper: positive (+) and negative (o) training examples on axes x₁ and x₂, separated by a straight-line decision boundary.]
(b) Explain any 2 hyperparameter you can tune to improve the performance of a neural network. (4 Marks)

Match the corresponding neural network component to its role in the neural network.
(i) Cross-Entropy (ii) Adam (iii) Mean Squared Error (iv) ReLU (v) Sigmoid (vi) Softmax (vii) Stochastic Gradient Descent (viii) Tanh (ix) Mean Absolute Error
a) Activation Function b) Loss Function c) Optimizer [9 points]

a) Draw and label a typical neural network
b) Explain in detail how a neural network learns. [10 points]

A set of data points is generated by the following process: Y = w₀ + w₁X¹ + w₂X² + w₃X³ + w₄X⁴ + ε where X is a real-valued random variable and ε is a Gaussian noise variable.
You use two models to fit the data:
Model 1: Y = aX + b + ε
Model 2: Y = w₀ + w₁X¹ + ... + w₉X⁹ + ε
State with reason the case for each of the scenarios that follows:
(i) Model 1, when compared to Model 2 using a fixed number of training examples, has a bias which is : (a) higher (b) lower (c) the same
(ii) Model 1, when compared to Model 2 using a fixed number of training examples, has a variance which is: (a) higher (b) lower (c) the same
(iii) Given 10 training examples, which model is more likely to overfit the data? (a) Model 1 (b) Model 2 [2 points each]

Suppose you are given the following classification task: predict the target Y ∈ {0, 1} given two real valued features X¹ ∈ R and X² ∈ R. After some training, you learn the following decision rule:
Predict Y = 1 iff w₁X¹ + w₂X² + w₀ ≥ 0 and Y = 0 otherwise
where w1 = 3, w2 = 5, and w0 = −15.
a) Plot the decision boundary and label the region where we would predict Y = 1 and Y = 0. [6 Points]
b) Suppose that we learned the above weights using logistic regression. Using this model, what would be our prediction for P(Y = 1 | X₁, X₂) ? (You may want to use the sigmoid function σ(x) = 1/(1 + exp(−x)).)
P (Y = 1 | X₁, X₂) =.......... [2 Points]

(a) With the aid of a diagram explain the principle of Gradient Descent algorithm. [2 points]
(ii) Write down the update formula for each iteration. [2 points]
(iii) Visualize and explain the effects of high and low learning rates. [2 points]
(b) What is a regularization term used for in machine learning? [2 points]

(a) Use (I) label encoding (ii) one-hot encoding for features of our dataset where we are interested in determine employment type of an individual, student, teacher, doctor and banker. Which approach is most suitable for the task [5 points]
(b) You trained a neural network model on the MNIST digit-recognition dataset. After evaluating the model on the test set, you obtained the following partial confusion matrix for the predicted digits 3, 5, and 8:
Actual 3: predicted 3 = 912, predicted 5 = 18, predicted 8 = 10
Actual 5: predicted 3 = 25, predicted 5 = 860, predicted 8 = 45
Actual 8: predicted 3 = 14, predicted 5 = 20, predicted 8 = 901
Using the matrix above, compute for the digit 5: (I) True Positives (TP) (ii) False Positives (FP) (iii) False Negatives (FN) (iv) True Negatives (TN) [4 points]

a. An old generation bank is trying to upgrade its services and enhance its customer retention capability using data analytics. One of their goals is to build a predictive model that determines whether a customer will abandon them and when it is likely to happen so that they can be proactive in their customer retention efforts. Being a friend of their Head of Operations, he has invited you to join the team to build the predictive model. However, all the banks have a record of their interactions with their customers over the last 30 years.
i. Describe the best practices that you may need to employ in trying to convert this customer interaction log into a dataset that can be used for machine learning given the following situations:
1. The log is a mixture of textual and numeric values. (1 marks)
2. The data contains a lot of missing values. Discuss your options and state which you will employ based on your stated assumption(s). (3 marks)
3. The numeric values in the record have very high ranges (maximum – minimum). (2 marks)
ii. After preparing your dataset, you discovered that there is no way to explicitly tell which customer is still with the bank and which ones have left. What class of Machine Learning (ML) algorithms could be helpful to obtain this information from your dataset? Give one example of an algorithm in this class of ML algorithms. (2 marks)
iii. Suppose you have decided what ML algorithm to use. How will you assess its performance and convince the bank that your model works? (2marks)
b. Derive the classification rules from the output of a decision tree presented in fig.-1: (6 marks)
[Fig.-1 in the original paper: a decision tree on Outlook (Sunny, Overcast, Rain), then Humidity, Temperature and Wind, with leaves giving HoursPlayed.]
c. Larah is to defend her choice for the customer churn prediction task. As Larah supervisor with adequate understanding of her choice of algorithm, list and explain two (2) points you expect her to mention? (4 marks)

a. Sarah is a graduate of the University of Ibadan. She applied for the role of data scientist at DataMart Nigeria after her program. She was placed on probe and given a customer churn prediction model for an online subscription service as task to develop. She decides to use a decision tree. After training the model on historical customer data, she notices something odd—her tree has grown excessively deep, with dozens of branches and tiny leaf nodes. At first glance, the model performs exceptionally well on the training data, predicting past customer behavior with near-perfect accuracy. However, when Sarah tests it on new data, the accuracy drops significantly.
i. Suggest the kind of problem Sarah is facing. (2 marks)
ii. Briefly explain the problem in your own words and state two (2) techniques to solve it. (4 marks)
b. How does pre-pruning compare to post-pruning in improving the generalization ability of a decision tree, and under what conditions does each method perform best? (4 marks)
c. Compare and contrast the following ML concepts: (10 marks)
i. Classification and Regression
ii. Supervised and Unsupervised Learning
iii. Parameters and Hyperparameters
iv. Model-based learning and Instance based learning
v. Shallow learning and deep learning

a. Mercy, a young student navigating her career path came across Random Forest algorithm. She then decides to build a weather prediction model using it. She trained the model on past weather data to classify days as rainy or sunny based on temperature, humidity, and wind speed. After evaluating her model, she notices something strange; some decision trees in the forest make very different predictions from others. She knows that Random Forest relies on bagging (bootstrapping + aggregation) and feature randomness, but she wonders how much individual trees actually agree.
i. How does increasing the number of trees in a Random Forest affect prediction stability and accuracy? Does adding more trees always improve performance? (6 marks)
ii. As an experienced student, explain to Mercy how final result is gotten from multiple trees for both classification and regression tasks. (2 marks)
iii. Mention two strengths and weaknesses of Random Forest. (2 marks)
b. Two occurrences during training remain unclear to Mercy. When she uses shallow trees (low max depth, fewer splits), the model performs poorly on both training and test data. It seems too simple and misses important patterns and when she allows deep trees with many splits, the training accuracy is nearly perfect, but the test accuracy drops.
i. How does Random Forest handle the bias-variance tradeoff? (6 marks)
ii. Does Random Forest need Pruning? Why or why not? (4 marks)

a. The table below is the confusion matrix of a phishing mail detection model. From the table, calculate the precision, recall, accuracy, and F1-score of the model. (8 marks)
Phishing (actual): Phishing (predicted) 43, Not-Phishing (predicted) 18
Not-Phishing (actual): Phishing (predicted) 24, Not-Phishing (predicted) 119
b. Gradient Descent is perhaps the most popular optimization algorithm in ML. Write the pseudocode of the Gradient Descent algorithm showing the necessary equations. (State any necessary assumptions). (5 marks)
c. Mention two other optimization algorithms used in Machine Learning. (2 marks)
d. Succinctly describe the sub-grouping under GenAI. (5 marks)
